target_customer: College students searching for off-campus housing and the landlords and property managers who list to them
problem: Off-campus housing search was fragmented across Craigslist and word of mouth, with no single trusted marketplace per campus.
business_model: Marketplace with listing fees from landlords and property managers, later leasing and rent payments

founders.name: Jason Okrasinski
education: University of Michigan, Ross School of Business
founders.background_notes: Listed as Jason Okra on YC; later co-founder and CEO of Wayline.

founders.name: Tim Jones
founders.background_notes: Later senior product manager at Apartment List and executive at ESW Capital and Beacon Software.

founders.name: Evan Dancer
founders.background_notes: Rails and Ember engineer; later engineering manager at Apartment List.

exit.reason: Company farewell page ends its timeline with The End in April 2018; the YC page says the team joined Apartment List in 2018.

competitors.name: Craigslist and Apartments.com
competitors.what: General rental listings that students used for off-campus search
competitors.traction_then: Dominant general listings; a university official compared Cribspot to them

competitors.name: RoomChazer
competitors.what: Roommate matching, sublease postings and property data for landlords (Milwaukee)

technical_complexity.rationale: A listings marketplace with per campus search and landlord tools was standard web engineering; the hard part was supply acquisition, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Local supply and demand could build a campus level network, but listings were easy to copy and landlords multihomed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apartment List later took on the team in 2018, per the YC page.

market_need_then: Students every year needed housing on short timelines and press at the time said the founders started after struggling with their own searches.

rebrands.why: Likely to go beyond Ann Arbor, but no source states the reason or date.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Michigan Daily, TechCrunch, VentureBeat and campus papers; claimed presence at 175 campuses.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional and campus press and a trademark filing in 2015, but no evidence of a durable national brand.

pivots.to: Cribspot Home, a leasing experience with virtual tours, online leasing and rent payments
pivots.why: Described in later company pages; no date or reason stated.

outcome_analysis: Cribspot grew out of a University of Michigan class project, raised a $660K seed in 2014 and reached many campuses, then shifted toward a leasing product. The company ended in April 2018 and the team joined Apartment List. The cause is not public in detail, and later rounds seen on aggregators are unverified, so the outcome reads as a soft landing without a clear failure story.
notes: Cause of the 2018 wind down is not public beyond the farewell page. Concentrate reports a later $50K add-on bringing seed capital to $680K; undated here. Aggregators list a $1.78M seed round in June 2016 and totals of $2.7M to $2.98M; these are unverified. Apartment List deal terms were not found. Competitor sources are undated aggregator or campus press items. Exit typed as shutdown to match Inactive status; the team joining Apartment List is stated only on the YC page.
